reviews.headline: Memory and optics de-gross on the CXMT and Hock Tan headlines while money rotates into hyperscalers; ASML, TSMC and Anthropic's investor day are the next tests.

ASML's margin beat meets a demanding buy-side bar while AI de-grossing rolls on into Anthropic's investor day; semis and memory money keeps rotating into Mag 7 cloud names, where GS PB now sees HF exposure at highs.

The AI trade's marginal variable is now credit, not demand: CoreWeave's 15% yield and an Anthropic Q3 without an ARR number drove the sixth-to-seventh straight SOX down day, Korea hit circuit breakers as the memory corporate bid disappeared, and TSMC's 'demand exceeds supply' print was judged against a beat-and-raise bar it did not clear on margins.

Positioning flushed, credit still the swing factor: PB data show long liquidation in semis and hyperscalers (memory already de-crowded), Jensen's CoreWeave defence bought a bounce but not a credit repair, and the squeeze moved to crowded software and internet shorts.

Into the first megacap prints the desks are long META and AMZN, short-ish GOOGL, and the CoreWeave trade is attracting its first long-only tourists while memory and semicap stay split between HF bears and LO bulls.

Weekend mail is about the mechanism, not the thesis: the largest tech sell skew in five years was hedge-fund de-grossing, semicap and Korea are where holders are least sure, and Apple, Mag7 and software are where the money hid.

Monday's bounce is a SemiAnalysis headline and a CoreWeave upgrade landing on a tape that just set a record for net selling of Info Tech; the desks still cannot name the clearing event, and the crowding has migrated into TXN, LRCX, WDC, META and MSFT while memory, HDDs and neoclouds trade on technicals.

Monday's SOX bounce had no sponsors (HFs the largest share of Jefferies' tech flow in two years, JPM's desk 'not seeing any real demand'), CoreWeave could not hold an upgrade, Elice's -32% Korean neocloud debut and SoftBank's 4-year-high CDS re-opened the funding wound, and the crowding is now explicit: long AMZN, META, TXN and APH, short NFLX, TEL and Ciena, with GOOGL and NVDA the new homes of the Mag 7 short book.

SPCX's 13GW and rising $/W, plus SMCI's pre-announcement, bring buyers back to AI hardware pre-market into a book that is short-heavy (GS Prime short leverage at the 99th percentile) and still selling (BofA record tech outflows, Taiwan -$26B MTD); META is being de-grossed into tonight and NFLX's crowded short paid.
Beat-and-fade morning: META's funding language, LRCX's guide and TSLA's capex cut undo Wednesday's SPCX/SMCI bounce; a de-grossed book that is barely short sells into Asia and the Middle East.
Funding fear turns the AI unwind into a de-gross: SOX -6.7% on META's raise and LRCX's WFE; desks see rotation into low-beta NVDA/AVGO and software, not capitulation.
After Thursday's rout, desks see a de-gross, not a capitulation: shorts covered in memory/storage, fresh shorts in software and META, and specialists start pitching NVDA and MU back.

Weekend desk mail calls October a sector rotation and HF de-gross, not capitulation: UBS PB sees semis de-risking bottoming and memory bought, but nobody wants to add before the mega-cap prints, the Fed and the midterms.
Neocloud funding fear replaces lab-ARR fear: Musk's 'debt markets shut' hits CRWV/NBIS, META's $95bn raise reads as a clearing event, and desks split on whether the AI-hardware de-gross is done.
Funding fear flips to 'clearing event': META/SPCX/AVGO financings and the Anthropic S-1 spark a record semis-ETF bid, but desks call it relief, not conviction, into GOOGL/MSFT/AMZN.

Hynix's 'sold out through 2029' extends the AI relief into memory, but desks call it supply abating, not fresh buying, and crowded test/HDD longs (TER, STX) got punished on beats into MSFT/GOOGL tonight.

The hyperscaler night split the tape: GOOGL becomes the funding short on a Search miss, MSFT stays the crowded long, crowded SaaS (NOW) unwinds, and a reported MRVL-LITE deal divides the optics trade.
The AI earnings night turned into a de-gross: INTC's crowded long breaks, AMZN is sold but defended, memory falls on good prints, and META/MSFT become the megacap hide.
Friday's tech de-gross turned systematic: desks keep defending AMZN and the hyperscalers on fundamentals, but crowded semis longs (INTC, AMD) and memory (Kioxia, SNDK) are where conviction is fading.

Tech enters November de-grossed but not capitulated: MRVL-LITE is now official (LITE favoured, MRVL questioned), GOOGL is the sentiment laggard, and desks call AMZN/NVDA the safer AI longs into AMD and AAPL prints.

Mail reaction to AAPL (margin and Services) and MRVL-LITE keeps tech de-grossed into the midterms; desks still rotate into AMZN and the 'no negative discovery' AI names while shorts build in AMD before its print.

The Democratic sweep turned the AI unwind into a rotation: desks buy hyperscalers that own capacity and sell semis, memory, neoclouds and AI power, while AMD/ANET beats fade and the MRVL-LITE spread widens.

AMZN.summary: GS's TMT trading desk saw heavy rotational flow on 4 Nov: broad buying of hyperscalers (installed compute) against supply in names that sell into or build data centers.

APP.summary: GS TMT sales: APP +20% pre-market on a strong beat and guide against tepid expectations, plus a new buyback.

AMD.summary: UBS's cash desk saw selling in INTC, NOW, CRWV, AMD and SNDK on 4 Nov against buying in NVDA, MSFT, AMZN, META and LRCX.

CRWV.summary: UBS PB saw muted hedge-fund flows despite Neoclouds -8.4% and Power -6.3%, i.e. HFs were not the main sellers.

NOW.summary: UBS's cash desk names NOW among the 4 Nov sells (with INTC, CRWV, AMD, SNDK) even as software overall was bought.

VST.summary: GS Research (relayed): the Texas gubernatorial result could drive negative reactions in VST, NRG, SRE, XEL, CEG and AEP.

SKHYNIX.summary: Jefferies' Asia TMT desk: crowded semis and hardware sold again on 5 Nov, Samsung -7.6%, Hynix -9.5%, Kioxia -13%, Ibiden -16%, Japanese semicap -10-23%.

QCOM.summary: Barclays thinks positioning was short into QCOM's print; auto upside does not change the story until the DC business shows in FY27 numbers.

ARM.summary: Barclays: ARM positioning leaned short into the print; numbers 'okay' but not enough while smartphone weakness drives royalties.

AAPL.summary: UBS's Ruple sees a flight to quality on 4 Nov into software and select hardware, with AAPL +6.4%.

MRVL.summary: UBS special sits says MRVL's fall since 28 Oct turned a 24% offer premium into an 8-22% discount for LITE holders.

SPCX.summary: Jefferies' Titu notes SpaceX and Tesla were hit hard after the Democratic sweep (FT: midterms cost Musk >$60bn) but she is not giving up fully on AI.

ANET.summary: Bernstein's specialist relays that ANET estimates move up (2027 EPS $5.61 to $6.18) without the multiple re-rating.

DDOG.summary: Barclays: DDOG was one of the most crowded software longs; the F4Q guide (25% vs buyside ~30%) drove a ~17% pre-market drop.

INTC.summary: SIG saw January rebound call buying in INTC (~10k Jan 75 and ~15k Jan 80 calls) after the ~29% post-earnings fall.

ALAB.summary: Barclays: ALAB fell ~7% after hours despite a 12% guide beat, showing no appetite to go up the risk curve in SMID semis.

LITE.summary: UBS's special-situations desk measures the LITE-MRVL spread at 12.7% non-annualised with a 58% breakeven probability, far wider than China-approval semi precedents (4.5%, 76%).

MU.summary: SIG saw 7k MU Feb 1050/1250 call spreads and 3,500 Dec 950/1020 spreads bought, a recovery bet against the memory selloff.

ON.summary: GS relays ON +3% pre-market on a slight beat and above-Street 4Q guide, AI data-center revenue disclosed at $180mn in 3Q and $620mn expected for 2026, plus the $600mn Ferric acquisition.

PLTR.summary: GS relays the muted PLTR reaction (-8% pre) as reflecting weaker forward indicators: US commercial TCV +11% y/y vs +153% last quarter, RDV +79% vs +124%, cRPO growth 88% vs 105%.

GOOG.summary: UBS TMI sales reads AAPL's Services guide as more fuel for the GOOGL Search bear case that resurfaced after GOOGL's print, with AI tools cannibalising search activity q/q.

BKNG.summary: UBS TMI sales: BKNG sentiment is washed out and the bar is low into tonight; a clean quarter could spark a relief rally, pecking order ABNB > EXPE > BKNG.

CIEN.summary: Jefferies notes CIEN -11.3% on the deal because it buys lasers from LITE for scale-across pluggables; Nokia is vertically integrated and unaffected.

NET.summary: Barclays' desk says investors are still long NET into the print (infra/security, the two favourite software areas), looking for ~37% growth and a guide implying 4Q acceleration.

DT.summary: Barclays' desk first take on DT (-): NNARR ~$70m in cc vs the low-$80m investors wanted; results unlikely to draw the longer-term investors it needs.

ORCL.summary: Rothschild's desk: ORCL -9% after a $10bn bond plus ~$10bn equity raise (equity at an 11% discount, 5Y at +275bp) a week after the investor day; the market is being asked for a lot of capital ahead of the ANT IPO.

LRCX.summary: Jefferies' global spec sales says semicap came under much greater pressure than analog in the US sell-off and expects the same in Europe.

MSFT.summary: JPM's TMT desk names MSFT the source of funds for the AMZN/GOOGL rotation despite calling it the cleanest hyperscaler print.

NBIS.summary: NBIS grouped with CRWV by JPM's TMT desk as a neocloud selling off on bond-market access.

OKTA.summary: JPM's TMT desk sees continued long selling across security software; OKTA hit on the S&P 500 migration (1.7m shares for sale effective 11/14).

TXN.summary: GS's TMT desk says investors are broadening into non-semis names not exposed to AI-disruption narratives, citing AAPL, SNPS, ADI/TXN/NXPI, SPOT, V/MA and EBAY trading well.

ADI.summary: ADI named by GS's TMT desk among analog names trading well as investors broaden out of AI; top inbound 'strength in analog semis?'.

TOKYOELEC.summary: MS sales: Tokyo Electron +5% on a big beat with record China sales and prepayments, FY OP guide at the high end of buyside; TEL raised 2026 WFE to $160bn and 2027 to $210bn+.

MEDIATEK.summary: Jefferies' Asia spec sales keeps MediaTek as a highest-conviction buy into risk-off: 55x this year but 26x 2027, V8 $2.5bn in 4Q26, Fubon FY27 EPS ~18% above consensus.

VRT.summary: Bernstein industrials think the market overprices midterm risk to data centers (~55-60% of the 430 GW pipeline in restriction-leaning states, stable since summer) and favour PWR, ETN, VRT, NVT, GEV among others.

AVGO.summary: Mizuho (via TMTB) sees the MRVL-LITE combination tightening laser/DSP supply and boosting pricing power for AVGO, CRDO, COHR and SEI; financing is the key issue.

CRDO.summary: Mizuho (via TMTB) lists CRDO among the scarcity winners from a MRVL-LITE combination.

KLAC.summary: KLAC appears on JPM's investor 'where to hide' list as leveraged to rising INTC spend.

SNDK.summary: JPM's semis specialist says SNDK (-13.5% on Kioxia fallout) actually sounded good on its own print.

RDDT.summary: JPM's internet specialist calls RDDT's move to a logged-in-only experience (a response to GOOGL AI Overviews) very messy: ~17% of logged-out DAUs must convert to keep revenue flat.

APH.summary: GS's TMT desk relays GS Research adding APH to the US Conviction List, with 2027 EBITDA 10% above the Street.

CRWD.summary: GS's TMT desk notes CRWD +3% pre-market on a Deutsche Bank upgrade.

META.summary: UBS's desk flags S&P cutting META's credit outlook to negative on capex/FCF uncertainty, alongside a growing Musk-driven META bear case.

UBER.summary: UBS TMI sales: gig sentiment is as bad as in recent memory; UBER has become a very crowded short in internet on AV fears, while long-only support stays sticky post-Ackman.

KIOXIA.summary: Rothschild's desk reads Kioxia -16% in Asia as a sign the memory selling is not done.

MCHP.summary: JPM's buyside survey scores MCHP at -3, the most short-leaning name in its print slate.

DELL.summary: GS's TMT desk lists DELL and HPQ lower in sympathy with INTC's PC-led miss.

FLEX.summary: Barclays desk says the feedback is that EMS names (FLEX, CLS) de-rated too much against strong demand, so investors may keep returning.

AIXA.summary: Jefferies semis specialist says AIXTRON's first power-electronics (GaN) orders are hugely incremental, since revenue drivers can now be opto and GaN, and the steady order guide implies well above the 800m consensus.

SAMSUNG.summary: Jefferies' Asia specialist says Samsung turned negative intraday on an OP miss and no added 2026 shareholder return, which some investors had hoped for.

SNOW.summary: Bernstein's crowding work finds software uncrowded vs history, but SNOW is now the most crowded name in its coverage, followed by DDOG, PANW, TWLO and OKTA.

NXPI.summary: Jefferies desk says NXPI's Dec-Q guide missed both the Street and a buyside bogey near $3.9bn; the stock is -7% after running +12% into the print.

ADVANTEST.summary: MS sales says Advantest's 2Q OP of 266bn beat BBG consensus of 218bn and the FY guide was raised to 967bn; the desk stays long, citing CPU as a third growth layer alongside GPU and ASIC.

STX.summary: JPM spec sales says investors treated the STX pullback as overdone and buyable, but a crowded long base leaves STX and WDC exposed to any further ramp slippage.

TER.summary: UBS desk is surprised by TER -6% after a beat-and-raise, citing bogeys near the top of the guide range and more long crowding than it had assumed.

CSCO.summary: UBS quant screen shows a +6.99 2-week long-crowding spike in Cisco, which the desk calls the most noteworthy move in hardware.

GLW.summary: BofA TMT: the GLW beat came from Enterprise Optical, with growth accelerating from 65% in 2Q to 84% in 3Q.

CDNS.summary: Jefferies desk: the CDNS print gave bulls (Q4 guide, FY raise) and bears (in-line Q3, weaker GM, light RPO) something each; still a P/E premium to SNPS.

TSM.summary: Jefferies desk relays Commercial Times: TSMC CoWoS pricing poised for another increase of up to ~20%, with packaging lead times extending.

TSLA.summary: TMTB relays Barclays upgrading TSLA to OW/$450 on improving core auto, energy storage and Robotaxi, with SPCX merger optionality on top.

SHOP.summary: Schilsky says SHOP has become a favoured long in many conversations after the META Muse checkout partnership, with expectations now somewhat elevated.

AMAT.summary: Meyers' buyside survey scores AMAT at +3 despite the semicap drawdown.

WDC.summary: Seidman says WDC (and SMCI) faded much better-than-expected results as risk appetite moved from memory/storage/semicap into consumer internet and software.

SPOT.summary: Seidman says SPOT beat on users and gross margin and showed staying power, with largely positive feedback on the catalyst path into year-end.

NFLX.summary: Seidman says NFLX feedback skews negative as double-digit revenue growth and margins are scrutinised against engagement woes and content spend.

BESI.summary: Silver says BESI's 11% order beat did not build conviction; investors still will not underwrite the longer-term memory (hybrid bonding) story, and ~11% short interest has not squeezed.

SMCI.summary: Ruple says robust SPCX and SMCI prints failed to shift the debate on AI-infrastructure durability into 2027.

BE.summary: Jefferies notes data-center reporters including BE stayed under pressure on Friday despite upbeat fundamentals, as tech only stabilised.

ASML.summary: Villani reads Elon's plan to accelerate chip production as a direct injection for long-lead-time semicap, ASML (EUV) and KLAC first.

IFX.summary: JPM's STM survey finds enthusiasm for European analog has faded since the April-June run; long-onlys treat STM and Infineon as trading stocks, and Infineon expectations already look full into its November FY guide.

TSEM.summary: TSEM fell ~7% on Tuesday on a SemiAnalysis note, while semicap lagged the semis rebound.

CRM.summary: Favuzza/Wong: Salesforce agrees to buy Braze for $47.50 cash (~58% premium, $5.66bn, ~5x CY27 sales), CRM -3% pre-market while SMID software (HUBS, KVYO) rallies; no change to FY27 guidance and FY28 not guided.

GEV.summary: BofA's Obin (Buy, PO $1,310) previews GEV 3Q with $21.0bn of orders (1.70x book-to-bill, +44% y/y) including 13GW of gas power equipment contracts; Vertiv's preview is titled 'getting over last quarter's speed bump'.

TEL.summary: Hardwick (via Rand): pushing TEL as an OW idea has been 'tough sledding' in a month of marketing, with interest only from value and activist investors; HFs clearly favour APH and view TEL as the likely pair short until it delivers on DDN and a few good quarters.

MDB.summary: Rand: investors want to see good prints or commentary before getting more involved on the long side in MDB, DT and ESTC; Jefferies lists DT as its software top pick into prints.

PANW.summary: Rand on security: investors still like the theme but worry valuations have run on 'Mythos' concerns while the numbers impact is far smaller, a high bar with downside risk and positioning likely to shift more cautious into prints; CRWD, AKAM, PANW, NET and FTNT are on 5-6 day relative underperformance streaks vs IGV.

SNPS.summary: MS raises SNPS PT to $574 (Overweight): the market still undervalues the AI revenue opportunity, with the stock on 25x FY27 EPS despite +18% in a month vs a 36x five-year average; Barclays' desk lists SNPS on a 6-day negative streak and Bloomberg-X attention is falling (Δz -1.3).

WOLF.summary: Digitimes (via Wigg): IFX extends its WOLF wafer deal to 8-inch silicon carbide; WOLF's Bloomberg-X attention is nonetheless falling fast (Δz -3.2) after last week's rally faded.

NVTS.summary: Blayne Curtis from OCP: 800V power was a common theme and NVTS's collaborations with NVDA and MCHP put it in front of customers ahead of the 2027-28 design cycle.

SMTC.summary: Blayne expects NPO to dominate the scale-up optical design cycle through 2027-28 with meaningful CPO adoption pushed to 2029 or later, a content uplift for MTSI and SMTC; NVDA's USFP and CSCO/ANET XPO designs suggest pluggables are more durable than investors expect.

CEG.summary: UBS derivatives: within AI, investors rotated into hyperscalers and quality is +10% MTD vs momentum -10%; Romano's preferred AI expression is the AI Power basket (UBXXVOLT) where positioning is cleanest after power dislocated from XLU on AI funding fears. Basket constituents are not listed in the mail; CEG is used here as the power proxy the wiki tracks.

PWR.summary: From Data Center World Expo Singapore: experts expect DC demand to accelerate in 2027, supply chain is the constraint, prefab/modular prioritized and the industry is converging on 800VDC with 2027-2029 deployment; read positive for PWR (grid), CAT and CMI; investors now ask which industrials carry neocloud vs hyperscaler exposure after the CoreWeave bonds.

HPE.summary: Barclays research also downgrades HPE to Equal Weight after a ~186% YTD run, seeing less upside in servers and storage as memory prices normalise.

AGX.summary: The construction conference recap includes Argan within strong multi-year end markets, with execution, labor and prefab as margin drivers. It provides no Argan-specific investor-positioning evidence.

TLN.summary: The PJM procurement discussion identifies Talen as a possible participant after large projects absorb some capacity need. This is a scenario, not a disclosed award or crowded-stock signal.

ESTC.summary: Lenschow returns from management meetings more confident in security adoption, search/GenAI and the medium-term growth path. This is research conviction, not observed ownership.

NVT.summary: Hawney identifies nVent as a preferred US AI/electrification exposure while seeing a less stretched sector setup. No nVent-specific position size is supplied.

DISCO.summary: The relayed phrase calls Disco a funding name while citing low valuation for long-term investors. Its direction is ambiguous; no long/short label is imposed.

SMIC.summary: Tokyo Electron meeting notes describe increasing SMIC/Hua Hong investment. This is a supplier read-through, not evidence of SMIC investor sentiment or ownership.

SANM.summary: Sanmina is included in positive Rising Tech Leaders conference commentary. The excerpt supports constructive management tone, but is insufficient to assign stock-specific crowding.

WMB.summary: Williams appears among the team’s fall top ideas. The sector backdrop still includes affordability and refinancing risks; the excerpt contains no stock-specific crowding measure.

AKAM.summary: The bull case is inexpensive edge inference and attractive steady-state contracts; the overhang is incremental capex and unclear near-term unit economics.

AEIS.summary: AEIS is included in Brett’s preferred equipment names. A preference alone does not establish crowding or new client demand.

observations.author: Joshua Meyers (relaying JPM fixed-income call: Thomas Egan HY, Erica Spear IG, Tarek Hamid)
observations.summary: JPM credit's read of CRWV: a financing challenge, not a solvency one; LTM EBITDA should rise from ~$4.4b (June 2026) to $7.3b by year-end and ~$20b by YE27 against ~$130b of contracted revenue, with SPV/credit-backstop options; CDS trades at a positive basis to bonds and NVDA is the key stress-transmission channel.
observations.excerpt: US HY TMT Credit Research: CRWV’s is a financing challenge, not a solvency one. The high-yield market is challenging for unsecured CRWV financing right now, but investors seem to underestimate the companies’ future cash generation
